gaps.sentence: He denied all knowledge of the ___ (APPEAR) of the documents.
gaps.explanation: The documents vanished, so the negative noun 'disappearance' is needed; 'appearance' means coming into view.

gaps.sentence: It was the most ___ (FORGET) trip of my life.
gaps.hint: negative adjective: too good to forget
gaps.explanation: 'Unforgettable' = impossible to forget; 'forgetful' describes a person who forgets.

gaps.sentence: The article was full of ___ information (ACCURATE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'information'
gaps.explanation: The negative adjective 'inaccurate' (in- + accurate) modifies the noun 'information'.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INTERVIEW) asked her some difficult questions.
gaps.hint: the person who asks the questions (-er = doer)
gaps.explanation: The interviewer asks; the interviewee answers. The suffix -er marks the doer.

gaps.sentence: The tracks become ___ after heavy rain (ACCESS).
gaps.explanation: Heavy rain blocks the tracks, so the negative adjective 'inaccessible' (in- + accessible) is needed.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'signs of'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: After 'signs of' a noun is needed: recovery (the -er of 'recover' becomes -ery).

gaps.hint: person needed: someone who installs wiring
gaps.explanation: An electrician is the person who works with electricity; 'electric' and 'electrical' are adjectives.

gaps.sentence: New technology has ___ the way we work (REVOLUTION).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: revolutionise. After 'has' the past participle 'revolutionised' is needed.
